findings.title: Icon-layer dirty check on total world-object count misses same-frame swaps
findings.detail: WorldComponentUpdate (Source/DungeonWorldComponent.cs:87-95) only redraws when the total number of world objects changes. Settlement.Abandon (Settlement.cs:445-455) removes the Settlement and adds an AbandonedSettlement, which is a plain WorldObject, not a MapParent. The count stays the same, so the unblocked tile's icon stays hidden. Settling with a caravan adds a Settlement and removes the caravan during long events, so an icon can probably stay drawn under the new colony. The check also rebuilds the whole mesh whenever a caravan forms or a pod launches. Compare world.worldObjects.MapParents.Count (WorldObjectsHolder.cs:59) instead: it is the same test IsBlocked uses, it changes in both cases above, and it ignores caravans.

findings.title: Eligible scans every world object for every candidate tile
findings.detail: Eligible calls world.worldObjects.AnyWorldObjectAt for each candidate tile, and that method walks the whole object list each time (WorldObjectsHolder.cs:363). Generation cost therefore grows with tiles x objects, both at world creation and when the mod is added to an existing save. Build a HashSet<int> of surface tile ids that have an object on them once at the start of Generate and check against it.

findings.title: Level tint is scaled by the current maxLevel setting, not the world's generated maximum
findings.detail: TintMat(comp.GetLevel(i), settings.maxLevel) uses whatever the slider says now, but existing worlds keep their levels when settings change (TUBAD_Settings_Generation_Desc). Lowering the setting turns every icon above the new max purple; raising it shifts the whole map toward green. Pass the max the world was generated with instead: save it in DungeonWorldComponent beside genVersion, or use the highest value in levels.

findings.title: Per-dungeon IsBlocked check is a linear scan, making each rebuild O(dungeons x map parents)
findings.detail: IsBlocked calls WorldObjectsHolder.AnyMapParentAt, and MapParentAt checks every settlement and site one by one (WorldObjectsHolder.cs:496-506). The layer rebuilds on every change in world object count (DungeonWorldComponent.WorldComponentUpdate), and there can be thousands of dungeons. Collect the occupied surface tile ids into a HashSet<int> once at the top of Regenerate and test against that in the loop.

findings.title: Patch XML depends on one specific vanilla list entry
findings.detail: The PatchOperationInsert is anchored on the li 'WorldDrawLayer_WorldObjects_Expandable'. It exists in Core's Surface PlanetLayerDef today, but if another mod removes or renames that entry the operation fails and logs a patch error. The file's own comment says list order does not matter, so a PatchOperationAdd to Defs/PlanetLayerDef[defName="Surface"]/worldDrawLayers cannot fail on this. No mod in the corpus patches worldDrawLayers.
